title: Multi Agent Collaboration Gets Persistent Compute in Bedrock AgentCore
gist: AWS added runtime instances to Bedrock AgentCore, a second compute option running agents on managed EC2 in the customer account for persistent sessions up to fourteen days with shared file systems and GPUs, complementing the existing eight-hour microVM sessions. It targets long-running, multi-agent, and accelerator-heavy workloads, with a break-even around 24% sustained CPU utilisation.

themes.theme: Persistent compute for long-running multi-agent work

insights.claim: AgentCore runtime instances give agents persistent EC2-backed sessions that can run for up to fourteen days with shared file systems and GPU-accelerated instance types, versus the eight-hour serverless microVM ceiling AgentCore launched with.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Removes the runtime-duration and stateful-compute limits that forced teams to maintain separate EC2 fleets for long agent jobs.
insights.quote: runtime instances give agents persistent EC2-backed sessions that can run for up to fourteen days

insights.claim: Multiple agents can deploy into a single runtime and collaborate on the same host through a shared session directory, calling each other as tools within a shared session rather than invoking each other's APIs for every handoff.
insights.speaker: Sebastien Stormacq
insights.so_what: Co-locating agents on one host with a shared filesystem reduces handoff overhead for multi-agent collaboration.
insights.quote: your agents can call each other as tools within a shared session, iterating autonomously until the job is done.
insights.locator: A few things that should make agent developers smile quote

insights.claim: Teams can bring frameworks such as CrewAI, LangGraph, LlamaIndex and Strands without changing their packaging model, using an @app.entrypoint decorator and either a zip file or container image, while reusing the same AgentCore APIs, identity and observability.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Framework-agnostic packaging and API reuse lower switching friction for teams adopting the new compute type.

insights.claim: AWS positions runtime instances as complementary to microVMs and encourages mixed topologies where an orchestrator agent on microVMs dispatches long-running work to workers on instances.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: The microVM-orchestrator plus instance-worker pattern is the recommended architecture for cost-and-latency-balanced agent fleets.

insights.claim: A new capacity provider primitive defines allowed instance families, OS, networking and storage as a contract between agents and EC2 capacity, letting AgentCore provision, patch and scale on the team's behalf and avoiding managing Auto Scaling groups, launch templates or AMI pipelines directly.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Abstracts EC2 fleet management behind a declarative contract, reducing infra ops burden for agent teams.

insights.claim: Runtime instances are billed at standard EC2 rates in the customer account plus a management fee, with a cost analysis suggesting a break-even at roughly 24% sustained CPU utilisation versus microVMs, which charge per vCPU-hour and per GB-hour with no management fee and can be cheaper for low-utilisation, idle-heavy agents.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: The 24% utilisation break-even gives a concrete rule for choosing instances vs microVMs to control agent compute cost.
insights.quote: a break even at roughly 24% sustained CPU utilisation for runtime instances

insights.claim: Microsoft has taken a similar approach through Azure Foundry hosted agents, provisioning per-session VM sandboxes with persistent home directories that restore state automatically when sessions resume, and supporting multi-agent runs across Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Both hyperscalers converging on persistent stateful agent compute signals this is becoming table-stakes infrastructure.
insights.locator: Microsoft has taken a similar approach paragraph
